name: back saw
definition: push-stroke hand saw whose thin blade is stiffened by a brass or steel back, for joinery cuts (tenon, dovetail, gents patterns).
reason: Axminster sells Back Saws as a category; the stiffened push-stroke form is neither panel saw nor backed pull saw (dozuki).
Tenon is a size and tooth pattern of the back saw, made by many makers: non-maker named form.
Dovetail pattern of the Western back saw: non-maker named form (Japanese dovetail saws stay under dozuki).
Small turned-handle back saw pattern: non-maker named form.

name: coping saw
definition: hand saw with a thin, fine blade tensioned in a deep U-shaped frame, turned in the frame to cut curves in wood.
reason: Sold under its own name (Lee Valley saw types); frame form differs from hacksaw and scroll saw.
A deeper-framed coping saw with pinless blades: same frame-saw form, a non-maker named form.
A piercing (jeweller's) saw is made for jewellery and metal-craft work: C4 by the step 28 note (memo section 9).

name: vertical panel saw
definition: wall-standing frame machine whose circular saw runs on a vertical guide to cut full sheets held upright.
reason: Axminster lists Panel Saws as a machine class; construction class changes the body (memo 4b.3).

name: reciprocating saw
definition: hand-held power saw with a long blade driven back and forth in line with the body, for demolition and rough cuts.
reason: Own Toolstation saw group; form differs from jigsaw (in-line blade, no shoe-guided curve cutting).

name: plunge saw [track saw]
definition: circular saw whose blade plunges down from a sprung housing and that runs on a guide rail for straight sheet cuts.
reason: Sold and compared apart from circular saws; plunge housing and rail fitting change the form (C10).
UK retail name for a fixed (non-sliding) mitre saw; sliding is an attribute of the mitre saw.

name: cut-off saw [disc cutter]
definition: hand-held engine or electric saw with a large abrasive or diamond disc behind a guard, for concrete, stone and steel.
reason: Own saw group at Toolstation; large guarded disc form, neither circular saw nor angle grinder.

name: contractor table saw
definition: table saw on an open stand with the motor hung behind the table, between jobsite and hybrid types.
reason: Rockler lists contractor saws as a class beside jobsite and cabinet; construction class is a kind (memo 4b.3).

name: straight-line rip saw
definition: industrial machine whose chain-driven bed feeds boards past a fixed blade to rip a straight edge.
reason: Grizzly lists Rip saws as a table-saw class (memo S16); feed bed changes the body.

name: single-edged pull saw [kataba]
definition: Japanese pull saw with teeth on one edge only and no back, for deeper crosscuts and rips than a dozuki allows.
reason: Woodcraft and Lee Valley sell kataba as a type; no tree kind covers it. Provisional like its siblings (C11, CV-27).

name: keyhole saw [pad saw, drywall saw]
definition: narrow pointed hand saw blade on a handle, for starting cuts from a drilled hole or cutting plasterboard.
reason: Lee Valley lists keyhole saws as a saw type; narrow unsupported blade differs from panel saw.

name: bow saw [buck saw]
definition: saw with a coarse blade tensioned in a bow or H frame, for crosscutting logs and timber.
reason: Lee Valley lists buck saws; a bow saw for logs is C1 (K-173 wood-cutting); pruning saws stay C2.
Toolstation's multi cutters are oscillating multi-tools (DCS355 already filed there).
The harvester notes no gap: patterns of the axe kind (K-173).

name: kindling splitter
definition: cast-iron frame with a fixed upward blade, into which a small log is struck with a hammer to split kindling.
reason: Sold as its own item (Roughneck); fixed-blade frame form is neither wedge, maul nor powered log splitter.

name: detail sander
definition: hand-held sander with a small triangular (delta) pad that vibrates, for corners and narrow areas.
reason: Own Toolstation sander group; pad shape and motion differ from random-orbit and belt sanders.

name: sheet sander [orbital finishing sander]
definition: hand-held sander with a rectangular pad moving in small orbits, taking a cut-down abrasive sheet.
reason: Sold apart from random-orbit sanders; rectangular orbital pad is a different form.

name: drywall sander
definition: sander with a large round head on a long pole and dust extraction, for plasterboard walls and ceilings.
reason: Long-reach pole form, sold under its own name by tool retailers.

name: oscillating spindle sander [bobbin sander]
definition: bench machine with an abrasive sleeve on a spindle that rotates and moves up and down through a table, for curves.
reason: Workshop machine sold under its own name; spindle form differs from belt and disc sanders.

name: belt and disc sander
definition: bench machine combining a sanding belt and a sanding disc on one motor.
reason: Combination machine listed as a class by a fetched seller (C-10), like the planer-thicknesser.

name: wall chaser
definition: hand-held machine with twin diamond discs that cuts parallel channels in masonry for cables and pipes.
reason: Toolstation sells it in the grinder family; twin-disc guarded form differs from the angle grinder.
A belt sander on a bench or floor stand: mount is an attribute on every kind (tree, C12).

name: biscuit jointer
definition: hand-held power tool that plunges a small circular blade sideways to cut slots for joining biscuits.
reason: Sold under its own name; plunge-cutter form; filed with routers as a slot-cutting power tool.

name: router table
definition: table with a router mounted beneath its top and a fence, holding the work to be passed over the bit.
reason: Toolstation workshop tools lists router tables; a work-holding table like the workbench (C1.6, K-190), not a part.

candidate: Drill bit and saw blade sharpener
reason: Sharpening system: machine or jig system for sharpening edges.

name: magnetic drill
definition: portable drill press on an electromagnetic base that clamps to steel, usually with annular cutters.
reason: Made only for the magnetic mount and its body differs (C12(a)); sold apart from pillar drills.

name: hand drill [wheel brace]
definition: hand-cranked geared drill with a side wheel and a chuck, for small holes.
reason: Tooled-Up lists Stanley 105 hand drill beside braces; geared form differs from the sweep brace.
A ratcheting ring on a combination spanner: attribute (HI-TORQ already filed at C1.2.3.01).

name: pipe wrench
definition: heavy adjustable wrench with a hook jaw and serrated teeth that bite round pipe.
reason: Own Toolstation spanner type; jaw form differs from the adjustable wrench.

name: basin wrench
definition: long-shafted wrench with a pivoting jaw for tap and fitting nuts behind basins.
reason: Plumbing type sold under its own name; jaw-on-shaft form.

name: box spanner
definition: tubular spanner with hexagon ends, turned by a bar through a hole.
reason: Own spanner type; tube form differs from ring and socket wrenches.
Cranked multi-size spanner for tap back nuts: a plumbing pattern under the basin wrench.

name: block plane
definition: small one-hand plane with a low-angle bevel-up blade, for end grain and chamfers.
reason: Woodcraft sells block planes as a type; compared by role like smoother and jack (memo 4b.1).

name: shoulder plane
definition: narrow plane whose blade spans the full width of the sole, for trimming rebates and tenon shoulders.
reason: Own plane type at Woodcraft; open-sided form differs from bench planes.

name: router plane
definition: plane with a cutter hung below a flat base, for levelling grooves and recesses to depth.
reason: Own plane type at Woodcraft; base-and-hanging-cutter form.

name: plough plane
definition: plane with a fence and depth stop and interchangeable narrow cutters, for grooves along the grain.
reason: Named by the harvester on the Woodcraft page; fenced grooving form. Page does not show it in the logged gave text (†).
Cambered-iron rough-stock pattern (Stanley No. 40): a pattern of the stock-removal role, under jack plane.
Short-bladed bench chisel: a pattern, not a form, so a non-maker named form.
Skewed-edge paring pattern; non-maker named form.
Traditional strong flat chisel pattern struck or pushed; named form under bench (striking) chisel.
Large struck socket chisel for timber framing; pattern of the striking chisel.
Socket against tang is handle construction, already in the bench chisel definition: attribute.

candidate: Slick, bent and crank-necked paring chisels
reason: Pushed paring patterns shown by Lee Valley and Woodcraft: non-maker named forms under paring chisel.
Bevel-sided bench chisel pattern; non-maker named form.
Spindle roughing gouge is a gouge pattern beside bowl and spindle gouges: non-maker named form.

name: rasp
definition: steel bar or blade with individually raised teeth, for fast shaping of wood and soft materials.
reason: Axminster sells Files & Rasps apart; the leaf names rasps but holds no kind; tooth form differs from cut files.
Stanley's perforated-blade rasp design: maker-bound named form under rasp.
Small file pattern sold in sets; non-maker named form under file (size is an attribute).

name: combination lathe-mill
definition: metal lathe with a milling head on a column over the bed, one machine for turning and milling.
reason: Grizzly lists combo lathe/mills as a class: combination machine kind (C-10).
Size class of the milling machine: attribute.
Brownells divides presses into single stage, progressive and shotshell: press patterns under reloading press.

name: club hammer [lump hammer]
definition: short-handled heavy double-faced hammer for driving chisels and light demolition.
reason: Own Toolstation hammer type; heavy double-faced head differs from claw hammer and sledgehammer.

name: brick hammer
definition: hammer with a square striking face and a chisel blade, for cutting and setting bricks.
reason: Own hammer type; face-and-blade head differs from claw and pein hammers.

name: ball-pein hammer
definition: engineer's hammer with a flat face and a rounded pein, for metalwork and riveting.
reason: Own hammer type sold apart; head form differs.

name: cross-pein hammer [Warrington]
definition: hammer with a flat face and a wedge-shaped pein across the handle, for starting pins and tacks.
reason: Own hammer type; head form differs.
Already a non-maker named form (dead blow mallet) under mallet.
Heavy straight-claw nail hammer: a claw-hammer pattern.

name: slater's hammer
definition: roofer's hammer with a pointed pick, a side nail claw and a blade for cutting and holing slates.
reason: Own hammer type; no generic kind covers its pick-and-blade head.
Brick hammer that holds replaceable scutch combs: pattern of the brick hammer.

name: sledgehammer
definition: long-handled heavy hammer swung with both hands, for demolition and driving stakes.
reason: Own hammer type; two-handed long-handled form differs from the club hammer.

name: punch
definition: hardened steel rod struck with a hammer to mark centres, drive pins or set nails.
reason: Highland and Axminster sell punches with hammers; a struck tool family no kind covers.
Cupped-tip punch for sinking nail heads: pattern of the punch.

name: nail puller [cat's paw]
definition: short bar with a claw tip driven under a nail head to lever it out.
reason: Sold under its own name; short claw-tip bar differs from the wrecking bar.

name: pry bar [flat bar]
definition: thin flat steel bar with bevelled ends and nail slots, for prising trim and boards.
reason: Tooled-Up sells pry bars apart from wrecking bars; thin flat form differs.
UK name of the wrecking bar (curved claw end): alias row.

name: lifting bar [pinch bar]
definition: long heavy straight bar with a chisel or point end, used as a lever to lift slabs and heavy items.
reason: Own bar type at Tooled-Up; straight lever form, no claw.
A slotted bar for drawing nails: the nail puller kind.

name: plasma cutter
definition: machine that cuts metal with an electric arc through a constricted gas jet, sold and compared with welders.
reason: Toolstation and Bigweld sell it in welding; no cutting leaf fits a thermal cutter, so filed with welding machines (†).

name: gas soldering torch
definition: hand-held butane or propane torch for soldering, brazing and heating in trade and repair work.
reason: General soldering equipment is C1 (jewellery torches C4, K-171); a flame tool unlike the iron.

name: saw stand
definition: folding or wheeled stand that holds a mitre or table saw at working height, often with outrigger supports.
reason: Sold with workbenches and trestles (Toolstation); a work support like the sawhorse (C1.6).

name: line laser level
definition: self-levelling laser projecting horizontal and vertical lines for setting out.
reason: Toolstation lists laser levels beside spirit levels; instrument type is the kind (memo 4b.4).

name: rotary laser level
definition: laser with a spinning head that sweeps a 360-degree level plane, read by a detector on site.
reason: Sold apart from line lasers; rotating form and site range differ.

name: optical level [dumpy level]
definition: telescope on a tripod that sights a level line onto a staff, for site levels.
reason: Own instrument type at Toolstation.

name: angle finder
definition: dial, bevel or digital gauge that measures and transfers angles.
reason: Own Toolstation instrument; measures angles, which square and marking gauge do not.

name: detector [stud, pipe and cable detector]
definition: handheld device that senses studs, metal pipes or live cables behind a surface.
reason: Own Toolstation group; instrument type.

name: moisture meter
definition: instrument that measures moisture in timber or building materials.
reason: Instrument type sold apart; trade measuring tool is C1 (K-147).

name: infrared thermometer
definition: handheld non-contact thermometer that reads surface temperature from infrared radiation.
reason: Sold as a trade inspection tool (K-147); instrument type.

name: inspection camera [endoscope]
definition: camera on a flexible probe with a screen, for looking inside walls, pipes and machines.
reason: Sold under its own name in detection tools; instrument type.

name: sound level meter
definition: instrument that measures sound pressure level in decibels.
reason: Instrument type on the Toolstation page; site and trade measuring (K-147).

name: clamp meter
definition: electrical meter whose jaws close round a conductor to measure current without breaking the circuit.
reason: Fluke sells clamp meters apart from multimeters; jaw form differs.

name: oscilloscope
definition: instrument that displays electrical signals as waveforms, handheld or bench (ScopeMeter is a Fluke name).
reason: Electronics-work instrument is C1 (K-147); ScopeMeter is a trade name, so the kind is generic (†).

name: single ladder [leaning ladder]
definition: one-section ladder leaned against a support.
reason: No sliding sections, so not an extension ladder; ladder form is the kind (memo 4b.5).

name: roof ladder
definition: ladder with wheels and a ridge hook, laid on a pitched roof.
reason: Made only for roof use with a hook; form differs (C12(a)).

name: tripod ladder [garden ladder]
definition: ladder with a single rear leg forming a tripod, for uneven ground and hedges.
reason: Ladders are C1 whatever the use; tripod form differs (reading of 'garden ladder' †).

name: engine stand
definition: wheeled stand that holds an engine by its block and lets it rotate for rebuild work.
reason: Toolstation jacks & stands group; vehicle-service tool is C1 (K-13); form unlike axle stand.

name: transmission jack
definition: jack with a saddle that lifts and holds a gearbox for removal and fitting.
reason: Own type on the jacks page; vehicle-service tool (K-13).

name: scissor jack
definition: jack lifted by a screw closing a diamond of linked arms.
reason: Scissor mechanism differs from trolley and bottle jacks; harvester's 'scissor stand' read as scissor jack (†).
Two-wheel hand truck with a drum cradle: pattern of the sack truck.
Two-wheel hand truck shaped for gas cylinders: pattern of the sack truck.
Cart that carries panels on edge: pattern of the hand cart.
Alias of the wheeled toolbox in the tree (tool trolley).
Hand-pushed platform or utility trolley is the hand cart.
Self-propelled tipping carrier for site material: the dumper (K-194).

name: backhoe loader
definition: wheeled machine with a front loader bucket and a rear digging arm.
reason: Self-propelled digging machine is C1 (K-194); two-ended form differs from excavator and loader.
Skid steer definition already covers wheels or tracks.
Forklift with a reaching mast: a forklift pattern (truck that lifts loads on forks).
Lift truck whose platform raises the operator with the forks: forklift pattern.
Pedestrian lift truck lifting on forks: the forklift kind; drive an attribute.

name: pallet truck [pallet jack]
definition: hand-pulled or powered low truck whose forks slide under a pallet and lift it just clear of the floor.
reason: Low-lift pallet mover differs from forklift (no mast) and from dollies; drive is an attribute.

name: tool chest
definition: drawered or lidded top box for tools, set on a bench or roller cabinet.
reason: Tooled-Up sells tool chests apart from roller cabinets; no casters, so its own container form.

name: site chest [jobsite box]
definition: large lockable steel box for storing tools on site or in a van.
reason: Own storage type; container form and security role differ from toolbox and chest.

name: tool pouch
definition: belt-worn pouch or holder carrying tools and fixings at hand.
reason: Worn container for one task's tools is C1 (K-132); differs from the tool bag.
A hard carry case is a portable toolbox; system membership is a C13 attribute (R-60 c).
A submersible pump rated for solids: solids handling is an attribute of the drainage pump.

name: surface pressure pump
definition: surface-mounted general-purpose pump that draws water and delivers it under pressure.
reason: General-purpose pumps are C1 (K-175); surface form differs from submersible and transfer pumps.
Chemical resistance is an attribute of the transfer pump.
Transfer pump with manual drive (drive is an attribute).
An abrasive disc cut for the angle grinder: grinding disc, abrasive build an attribute.

name: tungsten electrode
definition: non-consumable tungsten rod held in a TIG torch to carry the arc.
reason: Part made for TIG welders (K-12); not a filler rod, so not covered by welding rod.

name: brazing rod
definition: filler alloy rod or wire for brazing joints.
reason: Filler consumable like welding rod and solder (K-12).

name: soldering and brazing flux
definition: paste, liquid or powder that cleans joint surfaces for soldering or brazing.
reason: Consumable of soldering and brazing, filed beside solder by K-12 (†: K-12 names solder, not flux).
